title: Observation of Magnetosome Structures Isolated from Magnetotactic Bacterium Solidesulfovibrio magneticus RS-1
content: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) organize magnetic bacterial organelles (magnetosomes) as the geomagnetic sensor to achieve magnetotaxis. The inclination of the geomagnetic field could guide MTB cells’ swimming direction into a vertical direction. Combining magnetotaxis and aero/chemotaxis effectively allows MTB cells to find optimal growth habitats in chemically stratified aquatic environments [1, 2, 3]. MTB found in 13 phyla has morphologic and phylogenetic diversity [4]. The magnetosomes consist of a magnetite or greigite crystal enveloped by a phospholipid bilayer and magnetosome-associated proteins. The magnetosome-associated proteins synthesize, maintain, and functionalize the magnetosome organelle and are encoded in magnetosome island, a genetic region conserved in all MTB genomes identified. The magnetosome structures and functions of magnetosome-associated proteins have mainly been studied using model species of MTB belonging to Pseudomonadata phylum (Alpha-Proteobacteria).
